layout: One paper page per unit, boxes in this order: header (unit, can_do), words, pattern, my_sentences, check. Czech first, English after.

units.replaces_cheat_sheet_note: The current U6 cheat sheet teaches 'Vidím ženu. Mám psa.' and lists psa/muže/studenta; the v1.1 lessons teach café orders. This page follows the lessons.

can_do.cz: Objednám si jídlo a pití zdvořile.
can_do.en: I can order food and a drink politely.

words.en: Yes, we do. / Sorry, we don't.

pattern.name: What you order: the object form (accusative)
pattern.rule_plain: The thing you order or want is the object. Feminine words ending in -a change -a to -u. Words like čaj, pivo and chleba stay the same.

examples.en: I'll have a coffee and water.

pattern.preview: People and animals change too: Mám bratra. Mám psa. (Unit 8)

my_sentences_models.en: In the morning I drink coffee.

my_sentences_models.cz: Dám si polévku a chleba, prosím.
my_sentences_models.en: I'll have soup and bread, please.

notebook_steps.A_capture: Start your Unit 6 page. From memory, write the four café phrases you just heard. Then check.
notebook_steps.B_recall: Without looking, write two ways to order something. Then check.
notebook_steps.B_capture: In the Pattern box, write the rule in your own words. Then fill in: káva → ?, voda → ?, čaj → ?
notebook_steps.C_recall: Cover your page. Write the object forms of káva, voda and polévka. Then one line from Unit 5: what do you do? (Pracuju… / Studuju…)
notebook_steps.C_my_sentences: Write two true sentences about what you eat or drink.
notebook_steps.D_unit_check: Compare your page with the model page. Add anything missing, correct any mistakes, then tick your Check box.

units.replaces_cheat_sheet_note: Keeps the current U19 topic. Aspect is limited to five frequent pairs, as the reference description requires (perfective forms only for frequent verbs).

can_do.cz: Řeknu, co jsem dělal/a o víkendu.
can_do.en: I can say what I did at the weekend.

pattern.name: The past tense
pattern.rule_plain: Past = the -l form (+ -a for a woman, + -i for a group) plus jsem, jsi, jsme or jste. For he, she and they there is no jsem. Jsem never comes first in the sentence.

aspect_pairs.rule_plain: Two verbs for one action: the first is the process, the second is the finished result.

examples.en: I was cooking dinner for an hour.

examples.cz: Uvařil jsem večeři a šel jsem ven.
examples.en: I cooked dinner and went out.

common_mistake.right: Včera jsem byl doma. / Byl jsem včera doma.

my_sentences_models.cz: V sobotu jsem byla na výletě.
my_sentences_models.en: On Saturday I (f.) was on a trip.

my_sentences_models.cz: Včera jsem uvařil večeři a potom jsem četl.
my_sentences_models.en: Yesterday I (m.) cooked dinner and then I read.

notebook_steps.A_capture: Start your Unit 19 page. From memory, write five time words for the past. Then check.
notebook_steps.B_recall: Without looking, write three time words from Lesson A. Then check.
notebook_steps.B_capture: In the Pattern box, write the rule in your own words and the table for dělat. Then add být, jít and jet.
notebook_steps.C_recall: Cover your page. Write 'I was' and 'we went' in Czech (both genders for 'I'). Then one line from Unit 18: where do you live? (Bydlím v…)
notebook_steps.C_my_sentences: Write two true sentences about last weekend: one with a process verb, one with a finished one.
notebook_steps.D_unit_check: Compare your page with the model page. Add anything missing, correct any mistakes, then tick your Check box.
